findings.note: Supported conditional inference from the versioned baseline. Transaction counterevidence is explained, and alternate CE 7.4+ migration remains unvalidated.
Availability is separated from interchangeability. Implemented Dialect 2, index rebuilding, rolling documentation and the strongest case for retaining Redis are preserved.
Version-specific license options and unequal governance evidence support this limited conclusion; no legal fit, cost or support superiority is claimed.
Distinct publisher benchmark configurations and durability limits support workload validation. A Redis upgrade is explicitly a competing option; no head-to-head ranking or savings is invented.
Forward compatibility does not establish reverse recovery. Source isolation plus new target writes supports the illustrative data-path reasoning; AWS limits remain provider-specific.

prose.note: Accurately prioritizes the shared baseline, conditional replacement and separate feature/service proof; no universal winner.
Release numbers match dated captures and are explicitly not target recommendations; migration example versions stay visible.
Reasonable workload-risk recommendation from replication/persistence evidence; it does not claim any workload was tested.
Correctly distinguishes documented file incompatibility from possible but unvalidated alternative migration methods.
Feature availability and parity are separated; Dialect 2, index rebuild, query validation and rolling-module limits survive natural prose.
CRDT semantics and ordinary asynchronous replication are materially distinct; retaining the service is a conditional recommendation.
Inventory/testing advice is appropriate and the transaction counterexample is supported by the 8.0 behavior note.
The hypothetical transaction example is explicitly unexecuted and limited to a documented error-path change.
INFO identity fields and Lua module/static-linking history match the sources without assuming mandatory dynamic deployment.
Publisher attribution, Redis-to-Redis baseline and distinct numerical configurations prevent a false comparative ranking.
Matched-workload and recovery measurements are recommendations; explicit no-benchmark wording remains.
Both stores have documented WAIT/AOF limitations; recommendation does not imply tested equivalence or uniquely Valkey risk.
Ownership/cost dimensions are proposed comparisons, with AWS static parameters as a supported example and no established savings.
The validation checklist follows version and semantics boundaries; no test outcome is represented as observed.
Snapshot and cluster paths remain version-conditioned; writer fencing and state checks are advice based on asynchronous replication.
Post-cutover write recovery and reverse compatibility are appropriately separate from a documented forward path.
Illustrative order-status scenario is explicitly hypothetical and its unchanged-source premise entails the lost update.
AWS version pair and user requirements remain limited to ElastiCache; no upstream/newer-version guarantee is implied.
License boundaries match the saved vendor/tagged sources and rebut the blanket closed-source claim without legal deployment advice.
Formal Valkey policy is differentiated from Redis company self-description; no unsupported service/cost conclusions.
Open workload inputs and absence of benchmarking/restore/production compatibility tests are explicit scope limits.
Conditional pilot, retain and upgrade alternatives follow the findings; decisive dependency testing is a useful next step.
Prioritized thesis matches the presentation purpose and supported compatibility/recovery findings; licensing is motivation rather than proof.
Good progression from reconstructible cache to file and CRDT dependencies; edition, version and service identity remain visible.
Concrete application/search examples retain changed transaction behavior, implemented Dialect 2, rebuilding and rolling-release confirmation.
Rollback mechanism remains explicitly illustrative and correctly links post-cutover writes to recovery design.
Visual suggestion is editorial advice; numerical configurations, publisher attribution and non-comparability remain, with Redis upgrade as an alternative.
Strongest supported stay case is conditional; both stores durability caveats and cost uncertainty avoid one-sided promotion.
Date anchoring, walkthrough versions and exact AWS pair are retained for shortening; no fresh currency claim is made.
Explicit absence of benchmark, migration, recovery and cost evidence appropriately bounds what a presentation can promise.

assessment.note: Independent review of 21 source contexts, 38 facts, five findings, 22 report blocks and eight authored brief blocks. The authored brief provides a useful prioritized storyline for a 20-minute platform-engineering presentation, with concrete semantic and rollback examples, Redis retain/upgrade alternatives, and qualifications expressed in prose even without type labels. Original Search/WAIT Markdown, original Redis persistence HTML and retained browser contexts were inspected. Reused October 17 captures establish dated evidence only: no live refresh, chart-image validation, workload benchmark, cost model or migration drill. Three partial browser captures retain adequate context for their narrow claims; their documented HTTP 403 history is not treated as successful original-HTML access. No blocking objections.
